name: Send engineering daily digest to Slack with Jira, GitHub and OpenAI

parameters.content:
## Engineering Daily Digest

### How it works

This workflow runs every weekday at 9 AM, loads engineering digest settings, and collects Jira and GitHub signals in parallel. It finds recent Jira activity, stale in-progress Jira tickets, recent GitHub pull request activity, and stale pull requests without reviews, then normalizes and merges those findings. The combined data is summarized with OpenAI, formatted into Slack blocks, posted to Slack, and optionally logged to Google Sheets for velocity tracking.

### Setup steps

- Configure the weekday schedule trigger, including the intended timezone for the 9 AM run.
- Set the Config node values such as jiraBaseUrl, jiraProjectKey, staleTicketDays, staleReviewHours, repository list, Slack channel, and any sheet logging flag used by the workflow.
- Add Jira credentials with permission to search issues in the configured project.
- Add GitHub credentials or an API token with access to the repositories and pull request/search endpoints used by the workflow.
- Add OpenAI credentials and confirm the summarization model/prompt are appropriate for engineering digest content.
- Add Slack credentials with permission to post messages to the target channel.
- If sheet logging is enabled, add Google Sheets credentials and configure the target spreadsheet, sheet, and appended row fields.

### Customization

Adjust staleTicketDays, staleReviewHours, repository lists, Jira queries, the OpenAI summary prompt, Slack block formatting, and the Google Sheets logging toggle/columns to match the team’s reporting needs.

## Schedule and config

Starts the workflow on weekday mornings and defines shared settings used by the Jira, GitHub, Slack, and logging branches.

## Jira stale tickets

Queries Jira for stale in-progress issues and normalizes them into a digest-friendly format.

## Jira recent activity

Fetches Jira activity from the last 24 hours and converts the results into a consistent normalized structure.

## Merge Jira findings

Combines the normalized recent and stale Jira result streams into one Jira digest payload.

## Repository fan-out

Expands the configured repository list so GitHub checks can run for each repository.

## GitHub recent activity

Retrieves recent pull request activity from GitHub, flattens repository-level results, and normalizes them for the digest.

## GitHub stale reviews

Searches GitHub for stale pull requests without reviews, flattens the API response, and normalizes the findings.

## Merge GitHub findings

Combines the normalized recent pull request activity with the stale review findings into a single GitHub digest stream.

## Summarize and format

Merges Jira and GitHub data, generates an AI-written digest summary, parses the model output, and builds Slack message blocks.

## Post Slack digest

Publishes the formatted engineering digest to the configured Slack destination.

## Optional sheet logging

Checks whether spreadsheet logging is enabled, appends a velocity row to Google Sheets when enabled, or exits through a no-op branch when disabled.

nodes.name: Set Config Fields
nodes.notes: Single source of truth for everything the digest needs to run. Edit values here, nowhere else.

nodes.name: Fetch Jira Recent Activity
nodes.notes: JQL: project = {jiraProjectKey} AND updated >= -1d ORDER BY updated DESC

options.jql: =project = {{ $json.jiraProjectKey }} AND updated >= -1d ORDER BY updated DESC

nodes.name: Fetch Jira Stale Tasks
nodes.notes: JQL: project = {jiraProjectKey} AND status = "In Progress" AND updated <= -{staleTicketDays}d ORDER BY updated ASC

options.jql: =project = {{ $json.jiraProjectKey }} AND status = "In Progress" AND updated <= -{{ $json.staleTicketDays }}d ORDER BY updated ASC

nodes.name: Split Repository List
nodes.notes: Fans out Config.repos into one item per repo so the GitHub HTTP Request nodes run once per repo automatically.

nodes.name: Fetch Stale GitHub PRs
nodes.notes: GET /search/issues?q=repo:{owner}/{name}+is:pr+is:open+review:none — the review:none qualifier is the cheap way to find PRs nobody has reviewed, no per-PR calls needed.

nodes.name: Fetch GitHub PR Activity
nodes.notes: Native GitHub node — repository.getPullRequests (state=all). Classify opened/merged/closed in the next Code node.

nodes.name: Summarize Digest with OpenAI
nodes.notes: Native OpenAI Chat Complete — system + user prompts from Build LLM Prompt.

messages.content:
You are an engineering-ops assistant. You will be given JSON describing the last 24 hours of Jira and GitHub activity for a software team. Produce a concise daily digest as STRICT JSON only, no markdown, no code fences, matching exactly this shape:
{
  "whatMoved": "string, 2-4 sentences",
  "whatShipped": "string, 2-4 sentences",
  "whatIsBlocked": "string, 2-4 sentences, mention specific ticket keys",
  "needsReview": "string, 2-4 sentences, mention specific PR numbers/titles",
  "sprintHealth": "one sentence overall read, e.g. On track / At risk / Needs attention, with a short reason"
}
Only use the data given. If a category is empty, say so briefly. Do not invent tickets or PRs.

={{ JSON.stringify({ staleTicketThresholdDays: $('Set Config Fields').item.json.staleTicketDays, staleReviewThresholdHours: $('Set Config Fields').item.json.staleReviewHours, recentIssues: $json.recentIssues, staleIssues: $json.staleIssues, prsOpened: $json.prsOpened, prsMerged: $json.prsMerged, prsClosed: $json.prsClosed, prsAwaitingReview: $json.prsAwaitingReview }) }}

nodes.name: Post Digest to Slack
nodes.notes: Posts Block Kit JSON built upstream (messageType=block).
